_comment: STAGE-D per-batch coverage registry -- batch 'code_spec' (D17, Tier-2 frontend cluster)
(docs/twin_validation/wave2_6_unit_test_contract.md SS12.3/12.4; full-coverage program;
work-list docs/twin_validation/l3_release_package_unit_inventory.md D17).
Run via tests/harness/gate.py <this file> (L0+L1; calls tests/harness/coverage_audit.py) and
tests/harness/mutation.py <this file> (L2).
MODULE: frontend/code_spec.py -- the syndrome-code construction contract of the simulator
frontend: five frozen dataclasses (CodeQubit / PauliTerm / StabilizerCheck /
LogicalObservableSpec / Axis1StaticZZDeviceSpec) whose load-bearing __post_init__ coerces +
validates fields; the CodeSpec container (a big validating __post_init__ + to_manifest + three
properties data_indices / ancilla_indices / operation_set); and the Pauli-algebra function
commute. Axis1StaticZZDeviceSpec also carries to_metadata. The module imports NEITHER torch NOR
quimb (dataclasses + re + a metadata_guard/operation import that are numpy/math-free), so EVERY
public unit is CPU-PURE and IN-SCOPE for full L0+L1+L2 -- out_of_scope is therefore {} (the AST
reconcile refuses any gpu_bound claim on a torch-less module).
SEVENTEEN public units (AST reconcile _public_units_in_module: top-level public defs + every
public method of a top-level class + the load-bearing __post_init__ dunder of each frozen
dataclass). Every dataclass here HAS a __post_init__ (all five contribute one), unlike D16's
plain record carriers. CodeSpec's private _validate_qubits / _validate_checks_and_logicals
methods are NOT units (covered via CodeSpec.__post_init__), and the module-level private
helpers _as_terms / _require_unique_term_qubits / _require_record_token / _pairs / _pauli_vector
/ _pauli_product_in_stabilizer_span / _binary_row_rank are private -> not reconciled/scored, but
ARE exercised + mutation-covered through the public CodeSpec/StabilizerCheck/LogicalObservableSpec
construction paths (mutmut is coverage-guided). The unit set:
* 5 dataclass __post_init__: CodeQubit / PauliTerm / StabilizerCheck / LogicalObservableSpec /
Axis1StaticZZDeviceSpec.
* 5 dataclass to_manifest: CodeQubit / PauliTerm / StabilizerCheck / LogicalObservableSpec /
Axis1StaticZZDeviceSpec.
* Axis1StaticZZDeviceSpec.to_metadata.
* CodeSpec.to_manifest + 3 properties data_indices / ancilla_indices / operation_set.
* commute (the Pauli-algebra parity function).
CPU discipline. Every unit runs on plain-Python dataclass construction (no Stim, no simulator
run), so the tests are fast + deterministic. THE LOAD-BEARING PART is the commute Pauli-algebra:
commute is pinned against an INDEPENDENT symplectic recompute (X=(1,0), Y=(1,1), Z=(0,1); two
Pauli products commute iff the symplectic inner product over shared support is EVEN -- NOT the
module's own count-differing-bases expression) over a FULL enumerated single/multi-qubit truth
table PLUS a Hypothesis property, with an assert_discriminates variant that flips ONE factor's
basis so the parity flips (a mutant that changes the anticommute rule / the parity test dies).
CodeSpec's data_indices / ancilla_indices / operation_set are pinned vs an INDEPENDENT partition
computed from the constructed qubits/operations (NOT the module's property) with an
assert_discriminates wrong-split variant. Every to_manifest / to_metadata is pinned to its EXACT
dict (coords/keys coerced to lists; default coords=() -> []; the to_metadata calibrations-present
vs absent branch is exercised BOTH ways). PauliTerm.__post_init__ upper-cases basis (verified in
source: object.__setattr__(self, 'basis', str(self.basis).upper())), so a basis-CASE literal
mutant a callee normalizes is EQUIVALENT while a WRAP/semantic mutant is killable -- the tests
feed lowercase input and pin the upper-cased result to make the .upper() load-bearing.
RAISING-GUARD ROUTE COVERAGE (the D13 guard-route lesson): every validation raise is tripped
through EVERY input route that reaches it with the EXACT message via str(excinfo.value)==... --
the CodeQubit index/role guards; PauliTerm qubit/basis guards; StabilizerCheck name(empty/token)
/ancilla/empty-terms/dup-term/non-PauliTerm guards; LogicalObservableSpec name/empty-terms/index
/dup-term guards; the seven CodeSpec top-level guards (name / num_qubits / rounds / no-data /
no-ancilla / no-checks / no-logicals); _validate_qubits' out-of-range (boundary index==num_qubits
trips >= not >), duplicate-index, and data/ancilla role-mismatch raises; and
_validate_checks_and_logicals' duplicate-check-name, ancilla-not-ancilla, check-term-not-data,
checks-do-not-commute, duplicate-logical-name, duplicate-logical-index, logical-term-not-data,
logical-does-not-commute, and in-the-stabilizer-span raises. The Axis1 label string literals
(passed to metadata_guard) are killed by tripping the edges 'must be a sequence' and the
calibrations 'not declared' raises with their EXACT (label-carrying) messages.
STABILIZER-SPAN depth. _pauli_vector runs X/Y/Z terms through BOTH set-membership arcs (a rich
valid spec routes an X logical, a Y logical, and Z checks so {'X','Y'} and {'Z','Y'} are each
load-bearing), and the GF(2) rank / stabilizer-span check is exercised BOTH ways: a valid spec
whose logicals are NOT in the span (rank increases -> no raise) AND two in-span specs -- a
single-check logical (Z0Z1 == a check) and a PRODUCT-OF-TWO-CHECKS logical (Z0Z2 = z0 XOR z1,
which forces the multi-row XOR elimination to detect the dependency).
NO exemptions + NO out_of_scope: every unit is CPU-pure and every guard is REACHABLE through a
constructor route (checked, not assumed): the CodeQubit/StabilizerCheck coords generator runs
with non-empty AND empty coords; each raising guard is tripped; and the private helpers'
branches are entered/exited through the public construction paths.
